g.title: G
cluster_micro
cluster_meso
cluster_macro

frag_micro_component_size → frag_meso_component_size_entropy upward Fish in larger contact components exert stronger social attraction, promoting further aggregation and reducing the number of small components, which lowers component-size entropy.

frag_micro_component_size → wave_meso_component_mean_escape_alignment upward In larger components, social alignment with many neighbors can dilute individual escape responses, reducing the component's mean escape alignment.

frag_micro_component_size → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation upward Larger components encompass more diverse headings due to weaker local coordination, increasing the mean heading deviation within the component.
frag_micro_component_size → mill_meso_component_rotational_order upward Larger components provide more individuals to sustain collective rotation, enhancing rotational order.

frag_micro_isolate → frag_meso_centroid_pair_distance upward Isolated fish can act as outlying singleton components when local avoidance or escape separates them from neighbors; their centroids then sit farther from the main component centroids, raising the mean distance between component centroids at the meso scale.

frag_micro_component_shark_distance → frag_meso_component_size_entropy upward Components whose centroids are near a shark experience stronger escape pressure; this can cause uneven local splitting or merging across the school, changing how fish counts are distributed among components and thus component-size entropy.

frag_micro_component_shark_distance → frag_meso_centroid_pair_distance upward When some components are much closer to the shark than others, differential escape responses can push their centroids apart or pull them together, altering the mean separation between component centroids.

frag_micro_component_shark_distance → pol_meso_component_polarization upward A component near a shark may align headings more strongly as fish flee, while farther components retain social headings; component-level polarization can therefore depend on how close the focal component is to the shark.

frag_micro_component_shark_distance → frag_macro_component_count upward Many local component-shark encounters can induce localized breakaways and regrouping, which aggregate into changes in the number of connected components across the whole school.

frag_micro_component_shark_distance → frag_macro_largest_fraction upward If components near sharks split off or are stretched away from the main body, the share of fish in the largest component can shrink; thus local threat distance can shape macro fragmentation.

elong_micro_major_projection → elong_meso_component_aspect_ratio upward Fish lying at extreme projections along the school major axis can pull or compress their local contact components, changing the aspect ratio of component position ellipses.

elong_micro_major_projection → elong_meso_component_escape_alignment upward Fish at different major-axis projections may receive different social and threat cues, so their escape directions can bias how the component major axis aligns with the mean escape direction.

elong_micro_major_projection → elong_meso_component_axis_length upward Individuals positioned far along the school axis can extend the spatial spread of their contact components, contributing to longer component major axes.

elong_micro_major_projection → elong_macro_school_aspect_ratio upward Repeated extreme projections of individuals along a preferred axis can sustain or amplify whole-school stretching, affecting the school covariance aspect ratio.

elong_micro_major_projection → elong_macro_major_escape_alignment upward When fish at major-axis extremes also have escape directions biased along that axis, their individual spatial placement helps align the school major axis with collective escape direction.
elong_micro_mahalanobis_sq → frag_meso_mean_component_size upward Outlying fish create weak links and local separations that can reduce the average size of contact components as the school fragments.

elong_micro_mahalanobis_sq → elong_meso_component_axis_length upward Fish with extreme Mahalanobis positions can stretch their local contact component along the displacement direction, increasing the component's major-axis length.
elong_micro_mahalanobis_sq → pol_meso_component_polarization upward Fish far from the school center often have deviant headings, which can lower heading polarization within their contact component.

elong_micro_mahalanobis_sq → comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance upward Peripheral fish with large Mahalanobis distance alter local spacing patterns, shifting the component mean nearest-contact distance.
elong_micro_mahalanobis_sq → frag_macro_largest_fraction upward When peripheral fish pull away, the largest connected contact component can lose members, reducing its fraction of the school.

elong_micro_mahalanobis_sq → elong_macro_school_aspect_ratio upward Extreme individual positions contribute to the global spatial covariance, so their elongation dynamics can raise whole-school aspect ratio.
elong_micro_mahalanobis_sq → wave_macro_school_escape_coherence upward Fish with extreme positions may have delayed or divergent escape directions, weakening school-wide escape-direction coherence.

elong_micro_component_projection → frag_meso_component_size_entropy upward Fish at the extremes of an elongated component are more likely to split from the group, increasing fragmentation and thus component-size entropy.

elong_micro_component_projection → wave_meso_component_mean_escape_alignment upward Fish positioned at the leading edge of an elongated component tend to have headings more aligned with the escape direction, raising the component mean escape alignment.

elong_micro_component_projection → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation upward Fish at the tips of an elongated component have headings that deviate more from the component mean, increasing mean heading deviation.
elong_micro_component_projection → mill_meso_component_rotational_order upward Fish at the extremes of a component have larger tangential position components, contributing to higher rotational order.

wave_micro_escape_alignment → frag_meso_component_size_entropy upward Fish with high escape alignment move cohesively in the escape direction, reducing fragmentation and lowering component-size entropy.

wave_micro_escape_alignment → wave_meso_component_mean_escape_alignment upward A fish aligned with its escape direction can socially influence neighbors to also align, amplifying the component mean escape alignment beyond simple averaging.
wave_micro_escape_alignment → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation upward High escape alignment causes fish to deviate from the school's mean heading, increasing the component mean heading deviation.

wave_micro_escape_alignment → mill_meso_component_rotational_order upward Strong escape alignment disrupts milling behavior by directing motion away rather than tangentially, reducing rotational order.

wave_micro_requested_turn_abs → frag_meso_centroid_pair_distance upward Large requested turns can steer fish away from local neighbors and create divergent paths among subgroups; this dynamic separation increases the spacing between the centroids of resulting components.

wave_micro_requested_turn_abs → elong_meso_component_aspect_ratio upward Differential individual turn requests can shear and stretch a contact component by driving some fish to turn sharply while others continue; this distortion can raise the component position-covariance aspect ratio.

wave_micro_requested_turn_abs → wave_meso_component_turn_variance upward Individual requested turn magnitudes are the behavioral inputs that generate within-component variation in requested turns; stronger and more heterogeneous individual turn requests can increase the variance of requested turns across fish in a contact component.

wave_micro_requested_turn_abs → pol_meso_component_away_shark_alignment upward Strong requested turns can reorient a fish and, through local social coupling, reorient the component mean heading toward the away-from-shark direction, increasing component away-shark alignment.

wave_micro_requested_turn_abs → comp_meso_component_edge_density upward Abrupt requested turns can break nearby contact relations as fish move along divergent headings; within-component edge density can therefore fall when turn requests are large or spatially uneven.

wave_micro_requested_turn_abs → mill_meso_component_angular_momentum upward Asymmetric turn requests around a component centroid can generate tangential motion and a nonzero cross product of component-relative position and velocity, increasing component mean angular momentum.

wave_micro_requested_turn_abs → lead_meso_component_lagged_alignment upward Turn requests that propagate from fish to neighbors can make current heading changes resemble previous-step neighbor heading changes; this dynamic propagation raises component mean lagged heading-change alignment.

wave_micro_heading_change → wave_meso_component_escape_coherence upward Individual heading changes are the elementary turns that, when coordinated within a contact component, produce coherent component escape directions.

wave_micro_heading_change → wave_meso_component_mean_escape_alignment upward Fish that turn toward their escape directions raise the component mean heading-escape alignment; heterogeneous turns weaken that meso alignment.

wave_micro_heading_change → wave_meso_component_turn_variance upward Variation among individual heading changes directly contributes to the spread of requested turn behavior recorded at the component level.

wave_micro_heading_change → lead_meso_component_cascade_fraction upward The sign and timing of individual heading changes determine whether a component's subsequent turns match its earlier mean turn, shaping cascade fraction.
wave_micro_heading_change → wave_macro_school_escape_coherence upward Many small individual turns can collectively synchronize or scatter escape directions, affecting whole-school escape coherence.

fright_micro_state → wave_meso_component_escape_coherence upward Frightened fish adopt escape directions; if their fright episodes overlap within a component, they can increase component escape-direction coherence.

fright_micro_state → fright_meso_component_fright_edge_fraction upward Frightened fish create frightened-frightened contact edges when they remain near other frightened fish; local episodes thus shape the fraction of frightened edges in a component.

fright_micro_state → fright_meso_component_fright_position_corr upward Frightened individuals may cluster toward component edges or interiors during escape, so individual fright occurrence contributes to the correlation between fright and distance from component centroid.

fright_micro_state → pol_meso_component_polarization upward Frightened individuals align with escape directions, and their local concentration can raise the heading polarization of the surrounding contact component.

fright_micro_state → fright_macro_onset_rate upward Individual fish entering fright are the elementary state changes that drive the macro onset rate; local frightened fish can also trigger further onsets through social transmission.
fright_micro_remaining → wave_meso_component_escape_coherence upward Longer fright persistence prolongs directed escape motion, supporting more coherent escape directions among component members.

fright_micro_remaining → fright_meso_component_prevalence upward Longer remaining fright keeps individuals frightened across more steps, increasing the fraction of frightened fish within their contact component.

fright_micro_remaining → fright_meso_component_fright_position_corr upward Prolonged fright changes where frightened fish are located relative to the component centroid, altering the spatial correlation of fright.
fright_micro_remaining → pol_meso_component_polarization upward Sustained fright tends to align escape-related headings, which can increase heading polarization within a contact component.

fright_micro_remaining → comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance upward Frightened fish adjust spacing differently from calm fish, so remaining fright duration can shift the component mean nearest-contact distance.
fright_micro_remaining → fright_macro_school_prevalence upward Individual fright duration controls how long fish remain counted as frightened, affecting whole-school fright prevalence.
fright_micro_remaining → pol_macro_school_polarization upward If many fish remain frightened, their shared escape bias can raise global heading polarization.

fright_micro_nearest_fright_distance → frag_meso_component_size_entropy upward Closer frightened neighbors accelerate fright contagion, causing fish to flee in divergent directions, which increases fragmentation and component-size entropy.

fright_micro_nearest_fright_distance → wave_meso_component_mean_escape_alignment upward Proximity to frightened neighbors heightens individual fright, strengthening escape alignment and raising the component mean escape alignment.

fright_micro_nearest_fright_distance → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation upward Fright contagion from nearby frightened neighbors increases variability in individual responses, raising mean heading deviation within the component.

fright_micro_nearest_fright_distance → mill_meso_component_rotational_order upward Fright disrupts coordinated rotational motion, so closer frightened neighbors reduce the component's rotational order.

pol_micro_heading_deviation → frag_meso_component_size_entropy upward Fish with large heading deviations are more likely to break away from the group, increasing fragmentation and component-size entropy.
pol_micro_heading_deviation → wave_meso_component_mean_escape_alignment upward High heading deviation indicates misalignment with the group, reducing the component's mean escape alignment.

pol_micro_heading_deviation → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation upward A deviant fish can influence neighbors through social alignment, but since alignment pulls toward the group, the net effect may be to increase local heterogeneity, raising component mean deviation.
pol_micro_heading_deviation → mill_meso_component_rotational_order upward Large heading deviations disrupt tangential motion, lowering rotational order.

pol_micro_neighbor_alignment → frag_meso_centroid_pair_distance upward Neighbor alignment helps keep fish in coherent local clusters rather than diverging; stronger alignment can limit the separation between the centroids of distinct contact components.

pol_micro_neighbor_alignment → elong_meso_component_aspect_ratio upward Alignment with neighbors along a common heading can maintain directional cohesion while permitting spread along that heading, contributing to elongation of the component position covariance.

pol_micro_neighbor_alignment → wave_meso_component_turn_variance upward Local heading alignment couples individual turning responses: fish aligned with neighbors tend to make more similar turns, which can reduce variance in requested turns across a contact component.

pol_micro_neighbor_alignment → pol_meso_component_away_shark_alignment upward When individual fish align with their contact neighbors, a locally shared escape heading can spread across the component; this social alignment can turn component mean heading toward the away-from-shark direction.

pol_micro_neighbor_alignment → comp_meso_component_edge_density upward Fish that align with nearby neighbors tend to move together and preserve local contact neighborhoods; this can maintain more within-component contact edges and increase edge density.

pol_micro_neighbor_alignment → mill_meso_component_angular_momentum upward Aligned headings can coordinate tangential motion around a component centroid when neighbors share a turning direction, producing a nonzero component angular momentum.

pol_micro_neighbor_alignment → lead_meso_component_lagged_alignment upward Neighbor alignment makes a fish more likely to copy earlier heading changes of its neighbors; this lagged social copying raises component mean lagged heading-change alignment.

pol_micro_shark_proximity → wave_meso_component_escape_coherence upward Individual proximity to sharks can synchronize escape directions among component fish, leading to more coherent component-level escape vectors.

pol_micro_shark_proximity → pol_meso_component_polarization upward Fish closer to a shark experience stronger threat and may align their headings with nearby escaping fish, increasing polarization within their contact component.

pol_micro_shark_proximity → pol_meso_component_away_shark_alignment upward High shark proximity for component members can bias component mean heading away from the nearest shark, raising meso away-from-shark alignment.
pol_micro_shark_proximity → pol_macro_school_polarization upward If many fish are simultaneously close to sharks, their shared escape alignment can raise whole-school heading polarization.

pol_micro_shark_proximity → pol_macro_polarization_proximity_cov upward Individual proximity responses contribute to how school polarization varies with mean proximity across time, making micro proximity a plausible input to the run-level macro covariance.
comp_micro_degree → pol_meso_component_polarization upward Well-connected fish can transmit and reinforce heading alignment within a component, supporting higher component polarization.
comp_micro_degree → comp_meso_component_edge_density upward Fish with many contacts locally increase the number of realized edges within their component, raising meso edge density.

comp_micro_degree → comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance upward High-degree fish are surrounded by many close neighbors; their local crowding can lower the mean nearest-contact distance of their component.

comp_micro_degree → frag_macro_largest_fraction upward Fish with many contacts can act as local connectors; their presence helps maintain a large connected component and raises the largest-component fish fraction.
comp_micro_degree → comp_macro_school_clustering upward High-degree individuals create more neighbor-neighbor contact opportunities, which can promote triangles and increase global clustering.

comp_micro_nearest_contact_distance → frag_meso_mean_component_size upward Shorter local contact distances create more links that can merge fish into larger contact components, increasing mean component size.
comp_micro_nearest_contact_distance → pol_meso_component_polarization upward Close local contacts strengthen alignment interactions, which can raise heading polarization within a component.

comp_micro_nearest_contact_distance → comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance upward Individual nearest-contact spacing is the local quantity whose distribution determines the component-level average nearest-contact distance.

comp_micro_nearest_contact_distance → frag_macro_largest_fraction upward Local contact distances control graph connectivity, which can change the size of the largest contact component at the school level.
comp_micro_nearest_contact_distance → comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance upward School-wide mean nearest-contact distance reflects the aggregation of local nearest-contact distances across fish.

comp_micro_clustering_coefficient → frag_meso_component_size_entropy upward High local clustering indicates tight subgroups that can become isolated, increasing fragmentation and component-size entropy.

comp_micro_clustering_coefficient → wave_meso_component_mean_escape_alignment upward Strong local clustering amplifies social influence over escape responses, reducing the component mean escape alignment.
comp_micro_clustering_coefficient → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation upward High clustering promotes local alignment, reducing heading deviations and lowering the component mean deviation.
comp_micro_clustering_coefficient → mill_meso_component_rotational_order upward Tightly clustered fish can more easily coordinate tangential motion, increasing rotational order.

mill_micro_angular_velocity → frag_meso_component_size_entropy upward Individual angular velocity indicative of milling keeps fish in a cohesive rotating group, reducing fragmentation and component-size entropy.
mill_micro_angular_velocity → wave_meso_component_mean_escape_alignment upward Milling fish are oriented tangentially rather than toward escape, reducing the component mean escape alignment.
mill_micro_angular_velocity → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation upward Tangential orientation during milling deviates from the school mean heading, increasing component mean heading deviation.
mill_micro_angular_velocity → mill_meso_component_rotational_order upward Fish with high angular velocity contribute directly to the component's rotational order by moving tangentially.

mill_micro_tangential_speed → frag_meso_centroid_pair_distance upward Tangential motion around a common center can fling subgroups outward when social coupling is weak, increasing the spatial separation between component centroids.

mill_micro_tangential_speed → elong_meso_component_aspect_ratio upward Differential tangential speeds can stretch a component by moving fish at different rates around its center; this shear can increase the component position-covariance aspect ratio.

mill_micro_tangential_speed → comp_meso_component_edge_density upward Tangential shear can slide neighboring fish past one another and break contact relations; stronger differential tangential motion can reduce within-component contact edge density.

mill_micro_tangential_speed → mill_meso_component_angular_momentum upward Individual tangential speeds around the school centroid are the micro-level motion ingredients that, when expressed around a component centroid, aggregate into nonzero component mean angular momentum.

mill_micro_tangential_speed → lead_meso_component_lagged_alignment upward Coordinated tangential motion changes fish headings in sequence around a component, so later heading changes can match earlier neighbor changes and raise lagged heading-change alignment.

mill_micro_radial_velocity → mill_meso_component_angular_velocity upward Radial velocity changes fish distance from the component centroid and hence the weight of tangential motion, influencing mean component angular velocity.

mill_micro_radial_velocity → mill_meso_component_rotational_order upward Inward or outward radial motion of component fish can distort the tangential arrangement around the component centroid, affecting rotational order.

mill_micro_radial_velocity → mill_meso_component_angular_momentum upward Radial inflow or outflow modifies the spatial lever arm of fish around the component centroid, which can alter component angular momentum.

mill_micro_radial_velocity → mill_macro_school_rotational_order upward Coordinated radial motion across many fish can either support or disrupt a common tangential pattern around the school centroid, changing global rotational order.

mill_micro_radial_velocity → mill_macro_school_angular_momentum upward Radial velocities redistribute fish radii relative to the school centroid and therefore affect the school-scale cross product of position and velocity.

lead_micro_lagged_alignment → lead_meso_component_lagged_alignment upward Individual lagged alignment between a fish's turn and its neighbors' prior turns is the elementary propagation event that defines component mean lagged alignment.

lead_micro_lagged_alignment → lead_meso_component_cascade_fraction upward Fish whose own heading changes align with previous neighbor changes help make component turns sign-matched, raising the component cascade fraction.

lead_micro_lagged_alignment → lead_meso_component_influence_variance upward Heterogeneity in individual lagged alignment indicates uneven leader-follower roles, which can increase variance of influence scores within a component.

lead_micro_lagged_alignment → lead_macro_school_lagged_alignment upward The school-level lagged alignment is the collective expression of many individual fish responding to prior neighbor turns; widespread micro alignment supports the macro value.

lead_micro_lagged_alignment → lead_macro_school_cascade_fraction upward If individual heading changes frequently match earlier neighbor changes, the overall sign-matched cascade fraction across the school can rise.
lead_micro_influence_score → pol_meso_component_polarization upward Fish that strongly influence neighbor turns can align component headings, raising component polarization.
lead_micro_influence_score → lead_meso_component_cascade_fraction upward Influential fish can initiate heading changes that neighbors follow, increasing sign-matched cascades within a component.
lead_micro_influence_score → lead_meso_component_influence_variance upward Heterogeneous individual influence scores produce variance in influence among fish belonging to the same contact component.
lead_micro_influence_score → pol_macro_school_polarization upward A few influential fish can propagate directional changes across the school, contributing to global heading polarization.

lead_micro_influence_score → lead_macro_school_cascade_fraction upward Individual influence scores summarize who leads local turns, and aggregated leader effects can shape school-wide cascade fraction.
lead_micro_influence_percentile → frag_meso_component_size_entropy upward Influential leaders promote group cohesion, reducing fragmentation and lowering component-size entropy.
lead_micro_influence_percentile → wave_meso_component_mean_escape_alignment upward Influential leaders can initiate and coordinate escape responses, increasing the component mean escape alignment.
lead_micro_influence_percentile → pol_meso_component_mean_deviation upward Leaders provide clear directional cues that reduce heading variability, lowering component mean deviation.
lead_micro_influence_percentile → mill_meso_component_rotational_order upward Influential leaders can initiate milling behavior, enhancing rotational order within the component.
frag_meso_mean_component_size → frag_macro_component_count upward For a fixed number of fish, larger mean contact-component size implies that the school is divided into fewer components.

frag_meso_mean_component_size → frag_macro_largest_fraction upward When contact components are larger on average, a smaller number of components can contain a larger share of fish, raising largest-component fraction.
frag_meso_mean_component_size → wave_macro_school_escape_coherence upward Large connected components can support more coherent escape-direction transmission, increasing school-wide escape coherence.
frag_meso_mean_component_size → pol_macro_school_polarization upward Larger interconnected components support broader alignment interactions, which can increase whole-school polarization.
frag_meso_mean_component_size → comp_macro_school_mean_degree upward Contact components with more members tend to contain more recorded contacts per fish, raising the school mean contact degree.

elong_meso_component_escape_alignment → elong_macro_school_aspect_ratio upward Components whose major axes are aligned with escape directions can jointly produce a stretched whole-school shape, increasing the macro aspect ratio.

elong_meso_component_escape_alignment → elong_macro_anisotropy_index upward If multiple components stretch coherently along escape directions, their combined anisotropy can raise the whole-school anisotropy index.

elong_meso_component_escape_alignment → elong_macro_major_escape_alignment upward Component-level alignment between major axes and escape directions can propagate to the whole-school level when components share a common escape orientation.

elong_meso_component_escape_alignment → wave_macro_school_escape_coherence upward Components already elongated along escape directions can make escape vectors more coherent school-wide, linking meso shape alignment to macro escape coherence.

elong_meso_component_escape_alignment → pol_macro_school_polarization upward When component stretching is aligned with escape, fish headings within those components are more likely to be similar, raising global heading polarization.

elong_meso_component_axis_length → frag_macro_largest_fraction upward Component elongation often accompanies connectivity changes that affect whether the largest component retains a large fish fraction.
elong_meso_component_axis_length → elong_macro_school_aspect_ratio upward Elongated contact components contribute stretched member positions that can raise the whole-school aspect ratio.
elong_meso_component_axis_length → elong_macro_anisotropy_index upward Component-level major-axis length reflects directional stretching that can increase global positional anisotropy.
elong_meso_component_axis_length → elong_macro_major_escape_alignment upward If elongated components align with escape directions, their major axes can orient the whole-school escape alignment.
elong_meso_component_axis_length → wave_macro_school_escape_coherence upward Longer component axes can organize fish along a common escape line, supporting more coherent school escape directions.
wave_meso_component_escape_coherence → frag_macro_largest_fraction upward Coherent escape within components can keep fish moving together, helping maintain the largest component's fish fraction.

wave_meso_component_escape_coherence → elong_macro_major_escape_alignment upward Coherent component escape motion can stretch the school along that escape direction, aligning the school major axis with escape.

wave_meso_component_escape_coherence → wave_macro_school_escape_coherence upward When component members share escape directions, the aggregation across components can raise whole-school escape-direction coherence.
wave_meso_component_escape_coherence → wave_macro_escape_coherence_change upward Changes in component escape coherence propagate to step-to-step changes in school-wide escape-direction coherence.
wave_meso_component_escape_coherence → pol_macro_school_polarization upward Coherent escape directions within components align headings across the school, increasing global polarization.

fright_meso_component_fright_edge_fraction → frag_macro_largest_fraction upward Frightened-edge-rich components may either consolidate or break apart under escape, changing how much of the school remains in the largest connected component.

fright_meso_component_fright_edge_fraction → wave_macro_school_escape_coherence upward When frightened edges connect many fish with shared escape responses, the component-level clustering of fright can propagate coherent escape directions to the school scale.

fright_meso_component_fright_edge_fraction → fright_macro_school_prevalence upward Components with many frightened-frightened edges can sustain local fright spread, which can raise the overall fraction of frightened fish school-wide.

fright_meso_component_fright_edge_fraction → pol_macro_school_polarization upward Dense frightened-edge clusters tend to align fish toward escape, and multiple such clusters can contribute to higher whole-school polarization.

fright_meso_component_fright_edge_fraction → comp_macro_school_clustering upward Clusters of frightened connected fish can alter local triangle formation and contact clustering, contributing to global contact-graph clustering.

fright_meso_component_fright_position_corr → wave_macro_school_escape_coherence upward Clustered fright positions can make escape directions more locally shared, affecting the coherence of escape across the whole school.

fright_meso_component_fright_position_corr → fright_macro_school_prevalence upward Spatial clustering of fright within components affects how many fish become frightened overall, shaping school fright prevalence.

fright_meso_component_fright_position_corr → fright_macro_onset_rate upward When frightened fish are positioned near susceptible component members, new fright onsets can occur faster at the school level.

fright_meso_component_fright_position_corr → pol_macro_school_polarization upward Spatial correlations between fright and centroid distance indicate segregated escape responses that can alter global heading polarization.
pol_meso_component_polarization → frag_macro_largest_fraction upward Polarized components tend to move coherently, which can preserve connectivity and the largest component's share of fish.
pol_meso_component_polarization → elong_macro_major_escape_alignment upward Polarized component headings oriented away from threat can align the school's major axis with the mean escape direction.
pol_meso_component_polarization → wave_macro_school_escape_coherence upward Polarized components have more aligned headings, which can make escape directions more coherent at the school level.
pol_meso_component_polarization → pol_macro_school_polarization upward Heading alignment within contact components contributes to the global alignment of fish headings.
pol_meso_component_polarization → pol_macro_polarization_change upward Step changes in component polarization can drive changes in whole-school polarization.
pol_meso_component_polarization → lead_macro_school_cascade_fraction upward Highly polarized components transmit direction changes efficiently, supporting school-wide sign-matched cascades.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → frag_macro_largest_fraction upward Dense, high-degree components are more likely to remain connected or absorb nearby fish, increasing the fish fraction in the largest component.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → wave_macro_school_escape_coherence upward Highly connected components can propagate escape turns more effectively, increasing the coherence of escape directions at the school scale.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → pol_macro_school_polarization upward Dense components facilitate rapid heading alignment among members, and multiple dense components can collectively raise whole-school polarization.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → comp_macro_school_clustering upward Components with higher mean contact degree support more transitive contacts, and the mixture of such components can raise school-level clustering.

comp_meso_component_mean_degree → comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance upward Components whose fish have many contacts are generally more crowded; when such components dominate, the school-wide mean nearest-contact distance tends to decrease.

comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance → frag_macro_largest_fraction upward Dense spacing inside components affects connectivity between components and the fish fraction held by the largest component.
comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance → pol_macro_school_polarization upward Closer component spacing strengthens local alignment interactions, contributing to higher whole-school polarization.

comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance → comp_macro_school_mean_degree upward Components with smaller mean nearest-contact distances tend to have denser local links, raising school mean contact degree.

comp_meso_component_mean_nearest_distance → comp_macro_school_mean_nearest_distance upward Component mean nearest-contact distances aggregate across components to determine the school-wide mean nearest-contact distance.
mill_meso_component_angular_velocity → pol_macro_school_polarization upward Strong milling rotation implies tangential headings that can reduce global heading polarization.

mill_meso_component_angular_velocity → mill_macro_school_angular_velocity upward Rotational motion within contact components contributes to the mean angular velocity computed around the whole-school centroid.

mill_meso_component_angular_velocity → mill_macro_school_rotational_order upward Consistent component-level rotation can organize tangential directions across the school, raising global rotational order.
mill_meso_component_angular_velocity → mill_macro_school_angular_momentum upward Component angular velocity reflects local tangential motion that contributes to the school-level angular momentum.

lead_meso_component_cascade_fraction → wave_macro_school_escape_coherence upward Component cascades can synchronize escape turns across the school, increasing the coherence of escape directions at the macro scale.

lead_meso_component_cascade_fraction → pol_macro_school_polarization upward Cascades that align turning directions across components can also align headings globally, contributing to higher school polarization.

lead_meso_component_cascade_fraction → lead_macro_school_lagged_alignment upward When component turns propagate as signed cascades, individual turns become more consistent with prior neighbor changes, raising school-level lagged alignment.

lead_meso_component_cascade_fraction → lead_macro_school_cascade_fraction upward Components with many sign-matched cascade turns can collectively produce a higher whole-school fraction of fish matching the prior mean turn direction.

lead_meso_component_cascade_fraction → lead_macro_school_influence_variance upward Uneven cascade fractions across components imply unequal leader-follower influence, which can increase school-wide variance of influence scores.
lead_meso_component_influence_variance → pol_macro_school_polarization upward Heterogeneous influence within components can create conflicting turn initiations that alter global heading polarization.

lead_meso_component_influence_variance → lead_macro_school_cascade_fraction upward Components with heterogeneous influence can generate uneven turn propagation, affecting the school-wide cascade fraction.

lead_meso_component_influence_variance → lead_macro_school_influence_variance upward Variance in influence among component members contributes to the overall variance of influence scores across the school.
